title: Dedicated capacity hotfix and audit: hot-path scaling regression AAR
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Summary: During a production traffic spike on 2026-02-27 we observed a regression in dedicated-pool scaling for customer-dedicated fleets. Autoscaler failed to provision new workers within the SLO window, causing sustained token-level latency increases and transient 503s for several high-value customers. This ticket captures the immediate hotfix applied, verification steps, timeline, root-cause analysis, and a tracked set of action items to prevent recurrence and tighten operational controls.

Scope: hot-path scaling regression that affected dedicated pools across two regions, interactions between scale-controller backoff, placement sharding, and a new kernel selection optimization introduced in runtime-2.4. Not a model degradation event; workload request patterns amplified the regression.

Objectives: 1) Document what was done to restore capacity and validate correctness. 2) Produce an after-action report with prioritized engineering tasks, telemetry/alerting improvements, and a tested rollback/hotpatch playbook. 3) Create automated smoke tests and chaos scenarios for the autoscaler and placement sharding logic.
root_cause_summary: A recent optimization in kernel selection (runtime-2.4) changed the estimated GPU memory footprint under certain sequence-length distributions. The autoscaler’s placement heuristic treated some nodes as under pressure and triggered a conservative backoff; concurrently, the placement sharding picker prioritized certain racks, creating temporary hotspots. The combined effect delayed new-worker provisioning and caused request queueing beyond the SLO window.
mitigation_summary:
Hotfix steps applied 2026-02-27: 1) Disabled kernel-selection optimization flag for affected fleet tiers to reduce footprint variance. 2) Temporarily relaxed autoscaler minimum-provisioning thresholds for Dedicated high-tier customers. 3) Manually redistributed pending replicas across racks to eliminate hotspots. 4) Applied a short-term override to bypass backoff on 95th percentile scale operations. Result: capacity restored within 18 minutes and 503s dropped to baseline.
Verification: synthetic traffic replay against restored pools, token-latency traces, and KV cache hit-rate monitored for 6 hours post-fix. Metrics and logs attached in links.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible test in CI that simulates the sequence-length distribution and verifies autoscaler latency < SLO when kernel optimization is enabled
Autoscaler has an explicit safety override with guardrails documented and covered by unit + integration tests
Alerting: new alert when provisioning delay for any dedicated pool > 6 minutes plus runbook linked
Placement sharding has additional telemetry to detect rack hotspots and a mitigation pathway (auto-spread or manual ops override)
Rollback/hotpatch runbook validated in staging and run once in warm window
